html:
The Tjuroro, also known as the Jurruru, are an Aboriginal people of the Pilbara in Western Australia, in country along the upper Ashburton River.

Their neighbours on the map were the Thalanyji downriver, the Yinhawangka to the east and the Jiwarli to the south. Little is recorded about them. Sheep stations spread up the Ashburton from the 1870s and 1880s, and the language has since fallen out of use. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Tjuroro, also known as the Jurruru, are an Aboriginal people of the Pilbara in Western Australia, in country along the upper Ashburton River.
